message.content: {"items":[{"term":"lowkenuinely","definition":"To speak sincerely or share information in a calm, low-key way.","originContext":"Described as a TikTok-originated blend of “lowkey” and “genuinely,” used as a softer alternative to “actually” or “seriously.”","sources":[{"url":"https://preply.com/en/blog/2026-slang-definitions-and-statistics/","quote":"‘Lowkenuinely’ means to tell the truth or share information in a sincere, calm, or laid-back way."}]},{"term":"cortisol spike","definition":"A humorous expression for a moment of shock, embarrassment, or awkwardness.","originContext":"Reportedly began as a joke on X and later spread as a viral expression, often paired with an exaggerated cortisol-meter meme.","sources":[{"url":"https://preply.com/en/blog/2026-slang-definitions-and-statistics/","quote":"‘Cortisol spike’ is a viral internet joke used to describe moments of shock, embarrassment, or awkwardness."}]},{"term":"boy kibble","definition":"A joking name for a simple, high-protein meal, often made with ground meat and white rice.","originContext":"Presented as a playful counterpart to “girl dinner,” contrasting snack-like assortments with plain, protein-focused meals.","sources":[{"url":"https://preply.com/en/blog/2026-slang-definitions-and-statistics/","quote":"‘Boy kibble’ is a viral social media food featuring simple, high-protein meals, typically including ground meat and white rice."}]},{"term":"future faking","definition":"Making empty promises about the future to obtain something in the present.","originContext":"Described as a modern term for a pattern of behavior that may occur early in a relationship.","sources":[{"url":"https://preply.com/en/blog/2026-slang-definitions-and-statistics/","quote":"‘Future faking’ refers to a behaviour where someone provides empty promises for the future to get something they presently want."}]},{"term":"the saxophones are getting louder","definition":"A phrase signaling that something bad, negative, or inevitable is approaching.","originContext":"Linked to swelling saxophone music foreshadowing danger in the film Boyz n the Hood; online videos use it to signal impending doom.","sources":[{"url":"https://preply.com/en/blog/2026-slang-definitions-and-statistics/","quote":"‘The saxophones are getting louder’ means that something bad, negative, or inevitable is getting closer."}]}]}
